commitResults.messageBody: Rename the starter chatbot references to Buddy, update setup documentation, fill the local agent profile, and ignore compiled class files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Level 1 echo command loop
commitResults.messageBody: Read user commands continuously, echo non-bye input, and exit cleanly when the user enters bye.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Level 2 task storage and listing
commitResults.messageBody: Store entered task descriptions in memory and show numbered tasks when the user enters the list command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Level 3 task status commands
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce a Task class and support mark and unmark commands so Buddy can track completed tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Apply coding standard cleanup
commitResults.messageBody: Extract command helpers, keep task-number parsing explicit, and update the user guide to describe the supported commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Level 4 task types
commitResults.messageBody: Support todo, deadline, and event tasks using subclasses of Task so each task type controls its own display format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor task list management
commitResults.messageBody: Move task storage and lookup into TaskList so Buddy focuses on command flow while task bounds checking stays in one place.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add BuddyException for user-facing error messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduces a checked exception so command handling can signal invalid
input with a clear message instead of silently guessing what the user
meant (e.g. previously any unrecognised command was treated as a todo).

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle invalid commands and arguments with BuddyException
commitResults.messageBody:
Replaces the old fallback behaviour (any unrecognised input, including
bare "todo"/"deadline"/"event" with no arguments, silently became a
Todo) with explicit validation:
- unknown commands are rejected instead of being treated as a todo
- empty todo/deadline/event descriptions are rejected
- deadlines without "/by" and events without "/from ... /to ..." are
  rejected, with an example of the correct format in the message
- mark/unmark now report a specific reason for non-numeric or
  out-of-range task numbers instead of one generic message

TaskList.getTask now throws BuddyException instead of
IllegalArgumentException so its error message reaches the user the
same way as every other validation error.

Merge branch 'branch-A-Packages': organize classes into packages
Add support for deleting tasks (Level 6)
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds a `delete <index>` command that removes a task from the list. As
part of the A-Collections extension, TaskList now stores tasks in an
ArrayList instead of a fixed-size array, since deletion (and the
resulting index shifting) is handled naturally by ArrayList.remove()
and there is no longer a fixed capacity to track.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Save tasks to disk automatically (Level 7)
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds a Storage class that writes the task list to ./data/buddy.txt
after every command that changes it, and reads it back in on startup.
The save folder is created automatically if it doesn't exist yet, a
missing save file is treated as an empty list rather than an error
(e.g. on first run), and lines that don't match the expected format
are skipped with a warning instead of aborting the whole load.

Each task type now knows how to encode itself as a save-file line via
Task#toFileFormat(), overridden by Deadline and Event to append their
extra fields, mirroring how toString() already works for display.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Gradle support to package Buddy as a JAR (A-Jar)
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds build.gradle plus the standard Gradle wrapper scripts (gradlew,
gradlew.bat) so the project can be built without a separate Gradle
install, and packaged as an executable JAR via `gradlew jar`. Buddy
has no external dependencies, so a plain JAR with a Main-Class
manifest entry is enough to run with `java -jar buddy.jar`; a project
with third-party dependencies would need a "fat/shadow" JAR instead
to bundle those dependencies' classes too.

Verified by building buddy.jar, copying it into an empty folder, and
running `java -jar buddy.jar` from there, matching how the JAR is
expected to be distributed and run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
